title: Decongestion-driven continuous batcher and KV reclamation heuristics for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Mixed-length workloads (short prompts with long assistant responses and long prompts with short responses) cause uneven GPU memory pressure and tail-latency spikes when continuous batching coalesces incompatible sequences. Goal: Implement a decongestion-driven scheduling layer that proactively reclaims KV cache slices, prefers low-latency placement for short-interactive requests, and reduces memory amplification due to long-response jobs while preserving overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Tail P99 latency for short-interactive requests improves by >= 20% under the mixed workload synthetic benchmark compared to current baseline
End-to-end throughput degradation remains <= 5% for steady-state mixed workloads after enabling heuristics
KV cache eviction events remain bounded and measurable; reclamation strategy does not cause correctness regressions (no KV misses leading to inconsistent outputs)
Feature gated rollout with metrics in Console dashboards and automated rollback if memory watermark > 0.98 on more than 3 nodes in 10 minutes
design_notes: Introduce two watermarks for per-GPU KV allocation: soft_watermark=0.72 and hard_watermark=0.92. Soft watermark triggers background reclamation and preferential routing; hard watermark triggers aggressive preemption of low-priority long-response slots and immediate KV compaction.
Decongestion score per request = alpha * estimated_response_tokens + beta * (1 - recent_successful_prefetch_rate). Tunables: alpha=0.7, beta=0.3 initially; will be swept in experiments.

KV reclamation modes: 'soft-shed' (mark KV slabs for delayed eviction, continue serving) and 'force-evict' (immediate slab drop + graceful restart of in-flight long-request streams). Soft-shed attempts to compact contiguous KV regions asynchronously to avoid kernel-cold compaction pauses.

Scheduler changes: add a fast-path for short-interactive requests (< 64 prompt tokens and expected response < 128 tokens) to be placed into low-latency bins with pre-reserved KV slots; use a bounded coalesce timeout of 8ms for those bins to avoid wait amplification.

Preemption: when hard_watermark exceeded or decongestion score beyond threshold, preempt the oldest pending long-request batch if its estimated remaining generation time > preempt_threshold_ms (set to 15ms) to free KV region.
Metrics exposed: per-GPU KV allocation fraction, reclamation_rate (slabs/sec), preemption_count, short-bin_coalesce_latency_ms, P50/P95/P99 by request-length bucket, and end-to-end token cost delta.

Safety: all reclamation paths are idempotent and keyed; we maintain per-request KV versioning and fallback to reloading context from storage if a KV miss occurs. This is covered in the KV correctness e2e tests.
Configuration: feature-flagged rollout (runtime flag: 'decongestion-v1') with parameters adjustable from Console and via API for Dedicated customers.
Compatibility: ensure behavior consistent across quantized model variants; add small adapter to kernel allocator so quantized buffers follow the same watermarks to avoid silent OOMs.

Trade-offs: aggressive reclamation reduces tail but increases risk of cache churn and slightly higher token compute cost due to refetching; tuned to accept up to 3% token cost increase for a 20% tail latency reduction in target profiles.
experiments: Canary A/B on 10% of inference capacity vs baseline for 48h with synthetic mixed workload (50% short-interactive, 50% long-response) - collect P50/P95/P99, throughput, token-cost, and GPU memory watermark events
Parameter sweep: alpha/beta in decongestion score {0.5/0.5, 0.7/0.3, 0.9/0.1}, soft_watermark in {0.66,0.72,0.78}, hard_watermark in {0.88,0.92,0.96}, coalesce_timeout_ms in {6,8,12}
Long-running soak: enable on a subset of Dedicated clusters for 1 week to validate no regression in sustained throughput workloads (customer-sim workloads), monitor Console rollback triggers

Bench harness: extend existing mixed-length benchmark to simulate conversational turn patterns (think: user prompts 12 tokens, assistant 220 tokens; user prompts 420 tokens, assistant 30 tokens) and measure KV fragmentation and per-GPU free regions.
A/B validation metrics: require statistical significance (p<0.01) for P99 improvements before proceeding to broader rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge implementation behind 'decongestion-v1' flag; unit + integration tests green (ENG PR review required)
2) Internal canary on staging cluster with synthetic benchmarks (2 days)
3) Canary to 10% production capacity for 48h with automated monitoring alerts and rollback conditions
4) Parameter sweep adjustments and finalize recommended defaults; update runtime-1.22 release notes and config schema
5) Gradual ramp to 50% over one week; continuous monitoring of P99, token-cost, and memory watermarks
6) Full rollout with a 24h post-rollout verification window; revert immediately if more than 3 nodes exceed hard watermark within 10 minutes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager KV eviction increases token compute cost and can create oscillations. Mitigation: start with conservative soft_watermark and 10-minute damping window for repeated reclamation events.

Risk: Preemption could cause higher user-observed variance for long synchronous requests. Mitigation: preempt only when long-request expected remaining time > 15ms and mark preempted requests as lower priority for rescheduling into next available short-window bins.
Risk: Interaction with quantized model memory layout causing subtle OOMs. Mitigation: add cross-variant kernel allocator checks and run quantized variant soak where reclamation is exercised heavily.
Risk: Incorrect KV version handling leads to silent misses. Mitigation: add e2e correctness tests and a KV miss telemetry channel that triggers immediate rollback for notable error rates.
Risk: Console thresholds/alerts may not capture early regressions. Mitigation: create custom dashboard and PagerDuty runbook for decongestion flag activation.
